messages:
alex_csr: escalated — customer ACME (ticket #3456) reporting promo code SPRG24 returning 400 promo_inactive even though campaign start time was supposed to be 09:00 UTC this morning. multiple customers affected, some complaining credits never applied.

alex_csr: repro steps provided by customer:
```
POST /v1/promos/apply
{ "code": "SPRG24", "user_id": "acme_user_1023", "timestamp": "2025-11-04T09:12:03Z" }
Response: 400 {"error":"promo_inactive","message":"Campaign not active"}
```

alex_csr: customer says they saw successful claims yesterday in staging, then suddenly stopped today. ~80 support pings landed in last 2 hours. :grimacing:

deploy_bot: config-change detected — campaign_id=9876 modified by mira_ops at 2025-11-04T08:58:44Z. Fields: start_time="2025-11-04T09:00:00Z" -> same, redemption_cap=10000 (was 1000), cap_scope changed: "per_customer" -> "global". Change-id: cfg-20251104-9876

mira_ops: ugh, that was me. I was trying to bump the cap for a high-volume partner test and accidentally flipped scope to global. I didn’t intend to change scope. sorry, rolling back now.

jamal_engineer: thanks for flagging. Two issues here: (1) scope was set to global so system hit a different validation path (global caps are only enforced server-side after activation window) which may have confused active-checks; (2) I see the campaign start_time stored as "2025-11-04T09:00:00+00:00" in the UI but customer SDK submits local tz sometimes — need to confirm server parsing. Can you dump campaign row? need id, start_time, scope, redemption_cap, state.

mira_ops: pulling row now. DB row for campaign_id=9876: 
```
{ id:9876, code:"SPRG24", start_time:"2025-11-04 09:00:00", timezone:"UTC", scope:"global", redemption_cap:10000, redeemed_count:10015, state:"active" }
```

jamal_engineer: redeemed_count > redemption_cap — looks like off-by-one from earlier test bursts (burst claims bypassed limit due to a race in continuous batching). That explains why some calls return promo_inactive while others succeeded earlier. We need a quick rollback of scope -> per_customer and also adjust redeemed_count to min(redemption_cap, redeemed_count) or recompute per-customer totals.

alex_csr: customer impact: roughly 120 unique users attempted uses; about 35 expected to receive credit but got errors. They’re asking for immediate remediation and credits for failed users.

ryan_supportmgr: priority P0 for customer at risk. Jamal — can you run a patch? If DB change is risky, let's run a read-only script to recompute per-customer redemptions and then update scope back + fix counts. Also prepare communication and credits plan.

jamal_engineer: plan: 1) snapshot campaign row; 2) compute per-customer redemption totals for campaign_id=9876; 3) set scope='per_customer', set redemption_cap=NULL (we'll re-apply correct per-user cap of 1 later), set redeemed_count = sum(per-customer actual) to keep counters consistent; 4) deploy small fix to validation so promo_inactive only happens when now < start_time (avoid tz parse issues) 5) run smoke test. SQL I intend to run: 
```
BEGIN;
SELECT * FROM promo_campaigns WHERE id=9876 FOR UPDATE;
-- recompute per-customer counts
CREATE TEMP TABLE t AS
SELECT user_id, count(*) as uses FROM promo_claims WHERE campaign_id=9876 GROUP BY user_id;
-- update campaign meta
UPDATE promo_campaigns SET scope='per_customer', redemption_cap=NULL, redeemed_count=(SELECT coalesce(sum(uses),0) FROM t) WHERE id=9876;
COMMIT;
```

mira_ops: approved. I'll stand by to rollback further if needed. Please tag me before final commit.

jamal_engineer: executing now.

jamal_engineer: executed and committed. Logs: "updated redeemed_count -> 118, scope -> per_customer". Ran smoke test:
```
POST /v1/promos/apply {"code":"SPRG24","user_id":"test_user_1"} -> 200 {"applied":true,"credit_amount":50}
POST /v1/promos/apply {"code":"SPRG24","user_id":"acme_user_1023"} -> 200 {"applied":true}
```

qa_bot: quick regression tests passed for promo apply (end-to-end subset). No other campaigns affected in this cluster. :white_check_mark:

ryan_supportmgr: thank you. Alex — please grant 50 credits to the ~35 affected users and send wording for customer communications. We'll offer a goodwill credit for the disruption.

alex_csr: will do. Granting credits now and updating ticket with message draft. Draft: "Hi — we fixed a config issue causing SPRG24 to be treated as a global cap. We've reverted the campaign to per-user limits, applied a 50-credit goodwill to impacted accounts, and validated redemptions. Sorry for the disruption — let us know if any account still shows an error."

alex_csr: credits applied to 38 users (IDs attached to ticket). Customer updated and confirmed promos working. Closing internal postmortem ticket and creating a short playbook item to avoid scope flips in UI. :memo:

mira_ops: adding a UI guard so changing scope requires two-step confirmation. Also adding an audit lint to block accidental global flips for non-admin flows.

jamal_engineer: created PR to tighten validation and added a short migration to detect redeemed_count > redemption_cap anomalies. QA approved. PR id: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4121

alex_csr: marking this thread resolved. Thanks team.
